anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: Approved L1 is a small static voxel scene requiring discrete rotation and raycast mining with visible occlusion, lava/support hazards, and durability. Carbon d1 has three named isles and all useful home policies in hand, so it is mostly visible matching and independent placement. Carbon d2 adds staged target-versus-decoy choices and shared slack, but lacks the physical raycast/occlusion control problem.

evidence.explanation: Approved L1 activates four targets, one screen, one lava hazard, one support requirement, and durability two.
Generator creates blockers, target/cap geometry, hazards, and a rotation/raycast solution.
Runtime applies rotation and mining outcomes with occlusion, support, lava, and durability consequences.
Grader replays rotations/raycasts and checks hazards, durability, and final inventory.
Solver witness is a sequence of visible rotations and ray steps.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: Approved L3 requires continuous tilt control through physics, collisions, walls, wells, lamp order, hazards, and a minimum trajectory/control history. Carbon d2 has discrete card/research actions, persistent visible readouts, no motion-dependent observation, and no precision trajectory. Carbon network d3-d5 adds graph planning and resource dependencies but remains discrete planning rather than feedback control.

evidence.explanation: Approved L3 activates three lamps, three walls, three wells, physics coefficients, minimum ticks, and control changes.
Generator builds switches, walls, hazards, waypoints, and physics parameters.
Runtime advances velocity/position, handles collisions/hazards, and renders the timed loop.
Grader replays every event/tick and checks completion, lamps, minimum ticks, and controls.
Solver uses waypoint feedback and repeated controls.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: Approved L5 requires four changing swaps, at least seven waves, refill-preview reasoning, a forbidden candy, and exact terminal score. Carbon d5 is also high-dependency planning: an isle choice changes donor crews, tolls, reserves, and later budget. It is less temporally changing and less exact-score-like than Candy, so this is a structural high-end comparison, not empirical equivalence.

evidence.explanation: Approved L5 activates four changing swaps, at least seven waves, a five-cell refill preview, and one forbidden candy.
Generator enumerates changing-board routes.
Each visible swap triggers cascade, refill, score, and terminal-state changes.
Grader replays swaps and checks board/refill, score, waves, licorice, and exact completion.
Solver consumes a swap sequence whose later validity depends on earlier board changes.

visible_baseline_solution.visible_information: The screenshot shows five named isles with smoke and crew readouts, policy cards with title/description/effects/HOME destination, and a research pane with current stage, cost, and visible offers. HOME labels expose the card-to-isle mapping; no hidden identifier is needed.
visible_baseline_solution.decisions: Identify the two target cards already in hand, place each on its named isle, then advance through three research stages. At each stage choose the visible offer whose HOME name matches an unresolved isle, reject the decoy, and place the selected target. Preserve budget/turn slack and certify.
visible_baseline_solution.dependent_state: Research changes the visible offer set and hand; each placement removes a card and changes island readouts, budget, and turns. Wrong policies have adverse effects, while all target cards must be applied.
visible_baseline_solution.precision_and_control: Full mode uses one drag from a visible card to a matching map region per policy, plus research and certification buttons. There is no continuous trajectory, timing window, or frame-history requirement.
visible_baseline_solution.recovery: Invalid actions are rejected with feedback, but a valid wrong policy consumes state. Visible HOME labels and post-action readouts support recovery.
visible_baseline_solution.success_condition: The grader requires the expected full-surface transcript, all research stages, every target/home policy, all isles at emissions <= 0 and crews >= 100, generated budget/turn limits, and final certification.

evidence.explanation: Visible card, isle, and research markup.
Common placement/research updates.
Input binding, replay, and final checks.
Initial hand, staged offers, budget, turn limit, and goal.

baseline_judgment.rationale: Current d2/full is a discrete screenshot-planning task with five destinations, three state-changing research reveals, decoy selection, shared budget, and a multi-isle goal. It is more than d1's independent placements but lacks motion-dependent observation and precision control, and is simpler to operate than approved L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board. This supports L2 rather than a default L3; it is not a calibration claim.

findings.claim: Some ordinary-profile decoy and cost settings are generated as padding rather than exposed as active screenshot decisions.
findings.causal_explanation: D1 has no research and all targets fill the hand, so research_cost and its decoy cannot affect a valid solution. D2's six decoys include one initial decoy and three one-decoy research offers; remaining generated catalog cards are not offered by the staged UI. This does not invalidate the profile ordering, but the metadata overstates actionable decoys.

evidence.explanation: D1 has no research and d2 declares six decoys with three stages.
Only a minimum decoy count for initial/staged offers is required.
Hand/research slices and full catalog are separate.
Visible UI renders hand and current research offers, not an actionable full catalog.

findings.recommended_action: Optionally reduce inactive d1/d2 decoy metadata or document catalog padding; do not relabel solely for this issue.

concise_summary: Keep d2/full. D1 is independent visible matching; d2 adds staged target/decoy choices and shared slack; d3-d5 add network, branch, toll, and training dependencies. Both interaction modes preserve the generated problem and bind their own transcript surface. One low-severity source-proven issue is inactive ordinary-profile decoy/cost padding. No browser, evaluation, or parent runtime checks were run.
limitations: Historical pre-controls preservation is unavailable from the supplied source.
Absolute L1-L5 labels are source-based comparisons to three approved anchors, not measured equivalences.
No browser, multi-seed, grader, or exported-verifier runtime check was performed.
